model_annotation: The plot illustrates how accuracy (ACC) varies with the co-occurrence number for six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME). The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic scale with major tick labels at \(10^{1}\), \(10^{2}\), and \(10^{3}\) (with the axis extending from near 0 on the left to several thousand on the right); the plotted points appear at four increasing co-occurrence levels spanning from single-digit values to a few thousand. The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)”, is on a linear scale, and spans roughly from 38% up to about 66%, with regularly spaced tick marks every 5 percentage points (40, 45, 50, 55, 60, 65). The Base series is a gray solid line with circular markers, increasing from about 38.3% at the leftmost point to ~41.8% at the second, ~43.8% at the third, and ~44.0% at the rightmost point. FT is a blue solid line with downward-triangle markers, rising from ~39.8% to ~43.3%, then to ~46.1%, and ending near ~47.7%. IKE is a red solid line with upward-triangle markers, moving upward from ~42.8% to ~44.8%, then ~46.5%, and finishing around ~49.4%. MEND is a brown solid line with diamond markers, increasing from ~44.4% to ~48.8%, then to ~53.9%, and ending near ~56.4%. MEMIT is a purple solid line with hexagon-like markers, rising from ~43.7% to ~51.1%, then to ~52.9%, and ending around ~54.7%. ROME is a green solid line with square markers, increasing from ~51.1% at the leftmost point to ~57.2% at the second, ~62.3% at the third, and reaching ~66.1% at the rightmost point.
